messages:
maria: FYI scheduled EU firewall + IAM policy rollout in ~30m (14:00 UTC). Release note says deny-by-default for historic service accounts. This overlaps with GPU provisioning agents that use the old node role.
ashok: ack. which subnets / SGs are affected?
devin: looks like rule set 'eu-tight-2026-03' will block 10.32.0.0/16 unless we add exceptions. GPU warm pool nodes spin up from ephemeral autoscaling role that uses the old role ARN.
maria: exact change is: disallow egress to controlplane endpoints from private subnets unless they have the new role tag. rollout doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-iam-firewall.
sara: this will cause new GPU nodes to fail bootstrap (they contact keystore + provisioning API). We saw similar in staging last month. Warm pool should keep some capacity but size is small in eu-west.
ashok: can we add a short-lived exception for the autoscaler IP range (10.32.16.0/20) and the keystore endpoints until we complete role migration?
maria: ops asked for zero-exceptions policy but agreed to a one-hour maintenance window if we file a mitigation ticket. I'm proposing: (1) hold rollout in eu-west for 60m; (2) create scoped policy that allows node-provisioner role; (3) run canary for 10 mins. Agree?
devin: +1 to scoped policy. If we hold rollout we'll need to enforce cost guardrail - we can't leave warm pools oversized forever. Suggest set warm pool target to current size and disable scale-up during hold.
sara: I can patch the warm pool config for eu-west to target=2 and disable autoscaler for 45m. That reduces cost exposure.
sre-oncall: Are we ok with a fallback region? If provisioning in eu-west fails, traffic will spill to us-east which has limited spare GPUs and higher egress costs. We should annotate runbooks with cost impacts.
maria: yes, fallback enabled but throttled. We'll add a route that prefers local region. Also will signal for manual capacity increase in us-east if spill > 20% over baseline.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: starting canary: iam-rollout-eu->eu-west-1 (1/3 hosts) at 14:10 UTC. See http://deploys/3081234567
devin: canary logs show auth failures from provisioner at 14:12: "403 Forbidden: Missing role tag". Same as staging.
ashok: action items: 1) maria to pause rollout in eu-west (done?), 2) ashok to create temporary scoped policy for node-provisioner role, 3) sara to patch warm pool target and disable autoscaler, 4) devin to run quick role-tag migration script for the boot image.
maria: paused rollout in eu-west at 14:15 UTC. Filed mitigation ticket INFRA-8241 with the scoped-policy patch attached.
sara: warm pool patched: target=2 and autoscale disabled until 15:05 UTC.
devin: role-tag migration script pushed to S3, running on canary instances now. Logs look good, keystore auth succeeds after tag applied.
ashok: once canary is green, we'll re-run rollout in batches of 5 hosts and keep a 10-min observation window. Also let's add a monitoring alert for provisioning-failures > 5/min so we can abort sooner.
maria: agreed. also adding cost note to the ticket: estimated spill to us-east adds ~$1.2k/day if warm pools have to scale there.
sre-oncall: thumbs up. please keep channel updated when rollout resumes or if we need to failback.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: iam-rollout-eu paused by maria at 14:15 UTC. Canary rollforward cancelled.
maria: reopening at 14:40 UTC with scoped-policy; monitoring window 10m. Re-running canary now.
devin: canary passed, no auth errors for 12m. proceeding with batch 1/5.
sara: batch 1 done, new nodes booted and registered. no spill.
maria: rolling through batches. keeping autoscaler disabled until all hosts have new tag. ETA 15:05 UTC.
ashok: post-mortem TODO: add automated tag-injection during image build to avoid this class of rollout issues.
maria: noted. thanks everyone. closing thread when rollout fully complete.
